hook: Polymeric N3H2, a single-bonded nitrogen solid, was synthesized at about 139 GPa.
summary: Squeezing nitrogen and hydrogen mixtures to 134 to 139 GPa produced a solid made of chains of N6 rings, each carrying four hydrogen atoms and linked by hydrogen bonds. Synchrotron single-crystal diffraction located the hydrogen atoms directly, and Raman spectroscopy and calculations support the structure. The 7.98 kJ/g decomposition energy is an estimate, and the material was made only under extreme pressure, not recovered to ambient conditions.
title: High-pressure synthesis of a polymeric N3H2 solid stabilized by hydrogen bonds
